Related Theory $\mathrm{BrF}_3$ molecular geometry is said to be T-shaped or Trigonal bipyramidal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In an octahedral structure, the pair of $d$ orbitals involved in $d^2 s p^2$ hybridisation is:
questions.solution: $s p^3 d^2$ or $d^2 s p^3$ are hybridisation for the octahedral geometry. In octahedron, the bonds are formed parallel to the $x, y$, and $z$-axes, hence $d x^2-d y^2$ and $d z^2$ will be used to form the hybrid orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of following statements is not correct of sigma- and $\mathrm{Pi}-$ bonds formed between two carbon atoms?
options: Sigma-bond is stronger than a pibond
Bond energies of sigma-and pi-bonds are of the order of $264 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ and $347 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$, respectively
Free rotation of atoms about a sigmabond is allowed but not in case of a pi-bond
Sigma bond determines the direction between carbon atoms but a pi-bond has no primary effect in the regard
questions.solution: Bond energies of sigma and pi-bonds are of the order of $264 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ and $347 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ respectively as bond energy of sigma bond is greater than pi bond. Related Theory A sigma bond is stronger because of the head to head overlapping, while a pi bond is weaker because of side to side overlapping. A sigma bond requires more energy to break than a pi bond does.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Acetophenone when reacted with a base, $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{ONa}$, yields a stable compound which has the structure
questions.solution:
Key Idea : Aldehydes or ketones with $\alpha$-H atom, in presence of dilute base, undergoes aldol condensation to give $\beta$-hydroxy aldehyde or $\beta$-hydroxy ketone. On heating, aldols eliminate water molecule to form $\alpha, \beta$-unsaturated compound.
Note: When aldehydes condense with ketones, it is the $\alpha \cdot \mathrm{H}$ of ketone which takes part in condensation. This reaction is called crossed aldol condensation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In $\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}$ion, number of the bond pair and the lone pair of electrons on nitrogen atom are:
questions.solution:
Nitrogen forms a coordinate bond with Oxygen as it cannot have 5 bonds. Although 2 electrons are shared in a coordinate bond, the number of bond pairs is taken to be 1. Hence the number of bond pairs are 4 and the number of lone pairs is 0 .
The valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) model relies on the idea that electron pairs repel each other. This causes bonding and lone pair electrons to stay as far away from each other as possible. The electron pair repulsion gives rise to geometry of the molecules and compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not a correct statement?
options: Multiple bonds are always shorter than corresponding single bonds
The electron deficient molecules can act as Lewis acids
The canonical structures have no real existence
Every $\mathrm{AB}_5$ molecule does in fact have square pyramidal structure
questions.solution: The $\mathrm{AB}_5$ molecule does not have a square pyramidal structure but has a trigonal bipyramidal structure because of $s p^3 d$ hybridisation. Related Theory Benzene exist in canonical structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order in which the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length increases in the following is:
questions.solution: The bond Length decreases with increase of bond order which is the multiplicity of bond. If $\mathrm{BO}$ is 1 its a single bond; 2 for double bond and 3 for triple bond. The bond length of $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ is 147.5pm, in $\mathrm{O}_3$ is $128 \mathrm{pm}$ and in $\mathrm{O}_2$ it is $121 \mathrm{pm}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following the pair in which the two species are not isostructural is:
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{SiF}_4$ and $\mathrm{SF}_4$ are not isostructural because $\mathrm{SiF}_4$ is tetrahedral due to $s p^3$ hybridisation while $\mathrm{SF}_4$ has distorted tetrahedral geometry due to presence of lone pair.


Related Theory Two molecules are isostructural if they have a similar number of atoms arranged in a similar structure (spatial coordinates). Caution If they have same number of lone pair and bond pair, they are considered as isostructural.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has the $p \pi-d \pi$ bonding?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}$ has $\mathrm{p} \pi-\mathrm{d} \pi$ bonding. $\pi$ backbonding, is a concept in which electrons move from an atomic orbital on one atom to an appropriate symmetry antibonding orbital on $a \pi$-acceptor ligand. $\Rightarrow N, B$ and $C$ do not have $d$-subshell in valence shell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is bond order (b.o.) defined?
options: It is the sum of electrons in bonding and antibonding orbitals.
It is the difference between the numbers of electrons in bonding and antibonding orbitals.
It is the ratio of electrons in bonding to antibonding orbitals.
It is the average energy of bonding and antibonding orbitals.
questions.solution: The bond order is half the difference between the number of electrons in bonding (N<sub>b</sub>) and antibonding (N<sub>a</sub>) orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are there in the ground state electronic configuration of carbon?
questions.solution: The ground state electronic configuration of carbon [He]2s2 2p2 indicates two unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How are atomic orbitals expressed in wave mechanics?
questions.solution: The atomic orbitals can be expressed by wave functions (ψ ’s) in wave mechanics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the result of the electronegativity difference between the two atoms in a polar covalent bond?
questions.solution: In a polar covalent bond, the result of the electronegativity difference between the two atoms is that the bond becomes polar covalent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the condition for a molecule to be stable?
options: N<sub>b</sub> must be less than N<sub>a</sub>
N<sub>b</sub> must be equal to N<sub>a</sub>
The number of electrons doesn't matter for stability
questions.solution: A molecule is stable if the number of electrons occupying bonding orbitals (N<sub>b</sub>) is greater than the number occupying antibonding orbitals (N<sub>a</sub>).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the result of the electron density distribution in an antibonding molecular orbital?
options: It has no effect on the molecule.
questions.solution: The electron density distribution in an antibonding molecular orbital destabilizes the molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the significance of having orbitals with almost equal energy for hybridisation?
options: It allows for the formation of stable compounds.
It determines the type of atom involved in bonding.
It facilitates the promotion of electrons.
questions.solution: Having orbitals with almost equal energy allows for the formation of stable compounds through hybridisation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of force arises between the electrons of two atoms?
questions.solution: The repulsive forces arise between the nuclei of two atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How are stability and bond order related?
options: A positive bond order indicates an unstable molecule.
A negative bond order indicates a stable molecule.
A positive bond order indicates a stable molecule.
Bond order is unrelated to the stability of a molecule.
questions.solution: A positive bond order (N<sub>b</sub> > N<sub>a</sub>) signifies a stable molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of bond is formed when hydrogen is attached to a highly electronegative atom like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine?
questions.solution: When hydrogen is attached to a highly electronegative atom like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine, a bond known as a hydrogen bond is formed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is it necessary to use spectroscopic, X-ray diffraction, and electron-diffraction techniques to measure bond lengths?
options: Because these techniques are more accurate than other methods
Because they allow for the measurement of bond lengths in gaseous samples
Because they provide information about the bond's stability
Because they provide detailed information about the arrangement of atoms in a molecule
questions.solution: These techniques are used because they provide detailed information about the arrangement of atoms in a molecule, which includes bond lengths.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What molecular orbital has a node between the nuclei?
questions.solution: The pi (π) antibonding molecular orbital has a node between the nuclei.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the bond enthalpy of the H – H bond in a hydrogen molecule?
questions.solution: The value of the H – H bond enthalpy in a hydrogen molecule as 435.8 kJ mol-1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which theory is used to describe the overlap and hybridization of atomic orbitals in polyatomic molecules?
questions.solution: The valence bond theory is used to explain overlap and hybridization of atomic orbitals in polyatomic molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What condition must be met by orbitals when they are forming a bond?
options: They should have the same sign (phase) and orientation in space
questions.solution: The orbitals forming a bond should have the same sign (phase) and orientation in space.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of electron pair interaction has the second-highest repulsion?
options: It is not mentioned in the paragraph.
questions.solution: The repulsive interaction of electron pairs decreases in the order: Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) > Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp) > Bond pair (bp) – Bond pair (bp).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the other name for head-on overlap of bonding orbitals along the internuclear axis?
questions.solution: The Sigma (σ) bond is formed by head-on or axial overlap of bonding orbitals along the internuclear axis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the net charge of polyatomic ions typically assigned?
options: To a specific atom within the ion
To the atom with the highest electronegativity
To the ion as a whole
To the least electronegative atom within the ion
questions.solution: In the case of polyatomic ions, the net charge is possessed by the ion as a whole.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of the valence shell assumed to be in the VSEPR theory?
questions.solution: In the VSEPR theory, the valence shell is taken as a sphere, with the electron pairs localizing on the spherical surface at the maximum distance from one another.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How do sodium and chlorine achieve a stable octet of electrons, according to Lewis?
questions.solution: In the case of sodium and chlorine, Lewis describes the achievement of a stable octet by the transfer of an electron from sodium to chlorine, forming Na+ and Cl- ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens in the excited state of a Be atom to account for its bivalency?
options: One 2s-electron is promoted to the 2p orbital.
One 2s-electron is promoted to the 3s orbital.
One 2s-electron is promoted to the 2d orbital.
The 2s-electron remains in the same orbital.
questions.solution: In the excited state of a Be atom, one of the 2s-electrons is promoted to a vacant 2p orbital to account for its bivalency.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the bond length defined for covalent bonds?
options: The distance between the outermost electrons of two atoms
The distance between the nuclei of two atoms in a molecule
The distance between the innermost electrons of two atoms
The distance between the valence electrons of two atoms
questions.solution: Bond length for covalent bonds is defined as the distance between the nuclei of two atoms in a molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the result of sharing two pairs of electrons between two atoms?
questions.solution: When two pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms, it results in a double covalent bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is electron affinity defined?
options: The energy change when an atom loses an electron
The energy change when an atom gains an electron
The energy change when a molecule forms a covalent bond
The energy change when an ion is formed from an atom
questions.solution: The electron affinity is the negative of the energy change accompanying electron gain, which means it represents the energy change when an atom gains an electron.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the dipole moment of a polyatomic molecule calculated when it has multiple bonds?
options: By taking the average of individual dipole moments
By adding up the individual dipole moments as vectors
By subtracting the individual dipole moments
By multiplying the individual dipole moments
questions.solution: The dipole moment of a polyatomic molecule with multiple bonds is calculated by adding up the individual dipole moments as vectors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the electrons of a covalent bond when nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine is attached to a hydrogen atom?
options: Electrons are shifted towards nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine
questions.solution: When nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine forms a covalent bond with hydrogen, the electrons of the covalent bond are shifted towards the more electronegative nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the purpose of the Molecular Orbital (MO) Theory?
options: To understand the electronic configuration of elements
questions.solution: The Molecular Orbital (MO) Theory is one of the theories used to predict molecular shapes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of atoms are considered in bond enthalpy calculations?
questions.solution: The bond enthalpy calculations consider atoms in a gaseous state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which physical state is the magnitude of H-bonding minimum?
questions.solution: The magnitude of H-bonding is minimum in the gaseous state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do atoms combine?
options: To lower the energy of the system
questions.solution: Atoms combine because they have a tendency to attain the stable electronic configuration octet structure of the nearest noble gas in the periodic table.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is hydrogen bond defined?
options: It is the sharing of electrons between two hydrogen atoms.
It is the attractive force between two hydrogen atoms.
It is the attractive force between a hydrogen atom and an electronegative atom of another molecule.
It is the repulsive force between two hydrogen atoms.
questions.solution: A hydrogen bond is the attractive force that binds a hydrogen atom of one molecule with the electronegative atom (F, O, or N) of another molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the electronic configuration of carbon in its ground state?
questions.solution: The electronic configuration of carbon in its ground state as [He]2s2 2p2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What effect does the extent of distortion (polarization) of the anion have on the percent covalent character of an ionic bond?
options: It increases the percent covalent character.
It decreases the percent covalent character.
It has no effect on the percent covalent character.
It reverses the percent covalent character.
questions.solution: The extent of distortion (polarization) of the anion is a factor that determines the percent covalent character, suggesting that it increases the covalent character

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary factor that determines the shape of a molecule, according to the VSEPR theory?
options: The number of valence shell electron pairs around the central atom
The size of the central atom
The electronegativity of the central atom
questions.solution: According to the VSEPR theory, the shape of a molecule depends on the number of valence shell electron pairs (bonded or non-bonded) around the central atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the minimum requirement for each combining atom in Lewis dot structures?
options: To contribute at least one proton to the shared pair
To contribute at least one neutron to the shared pair
To contribute at least one electron to the shared pair
To contribute at least one electron and one proton to the shared pair
questions.solution: Each combining atom must contribute at least one electron to the shared pair in Lewis dot structures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the result of hybridisation in terms of orbital energies and shape?
options: Formation of orbitals with equivalent energies and shape
questions.solution: Hybridisation results in the formation of new orbitals with equivalent energies and shape.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why are molecular orbitals difficult to obtain directly from the Schrödinger wave equation?
options: Because the Schrödinger wave equation cannot be solved for systems with multiple electrons
Because they involve spin properties of electrons
questions.solution: The molecular orbitals are difficult to obtain directly from the Schrödinger wave equation because it cannot be solved for systems containing more than one electron.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of hydrogen bond is commonly observed in water molecules?
questions.solution: Water molecules commonly exhibit intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the theoretical limitation of the VSEPR theory?
options: It cannot explain the geometry of simple molecules.
It is based on quantum mechanical principles.
questions.solution: The VSEPR theory gives the geometry of simple molecules but theoretically does not explain them.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why does the second O – H bond in polyatomic molecules like ethanol and water show a difference in energy compared to the first O – H bond?
options: Due to changes in the chemical environment
Due to differences in the number of bonds
questions.solution: The second O – H bond in polyatomic molecules like ethanol and water shows a difference in energy because of changes in the chemical environment.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the specific goal of atoms in chemical bonding, as per the electronic theory?
options: To gain or lose all their electrons
To have a full octet of electrons in their valence shells
To have no electrons in their valence shells
To share their electrons with other atoms
questions.solution: The goal of atoms in chemical bonding, according to the electronic theory, is to have an octet in their valence shells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which types of orbitals are present in the third period elements?
questions.solution: The elements in the third period contain d orbitals in addition to s and p orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the value of the bond dissociation enthalpy for the dissociation of HCl into H and Cl atoms?
questions.solution: The value of the bond  dissociation enthalpy (∆aH⊖) as 431.0 kJ mol-1 for the dissociation of HCl into H and Cl atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In chemistry, how is the presence of dipole moment represented on a Lewis structure?
options: A small arrow with a cross on the positive end
A small arrow with a cross on the negative end
A crossed arrow with a cross on the positive end
A crossed arrow with a cross on the negative end
questions.solution: In chemistry, the presence of dipole moment is represented by a crossed arrow on the Lewis structure of the molecule, with the cross on the positive end.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What kind of forces exist between ions of like charge?
questions.solution: Repulsive forces exist between ions of like charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What factors does the formation of ionic compounds primarily depend upon?
options: The atomic number of the elements
The ease of formation of positive and negative ions
questions.solution: The formation of ionic compounds primarily depends upon the ease of formation of positive and negative ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does the formation of a negative ion occur?
options: Addition of protons to the neutral atom
Addition of neutrons to the neutral atom
Removal of electron(s) from the neutral atom
Addition of electron(s) to the neutral atom
questions.solution: The formation of a negative ion involves the addition of electron(s) to the neutral atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What shape do the orbitals formed due to sidewise overlapping have in the case of a pi (π) bond?
questions.solution: The orbitals formed due to sidewise overlapping in the case of a pi (π) bond as consisting of two saucer-type charged clouds above and below the plane of the participating atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How can you determine the group valence of an element based on Lewis symbols?
options: By counting the number of protons
By adding the number of valence electrons and inner shell electrons
By subtracting the atomic number from the number of dots
By either counting the number of dots or calculating 8 minus the number of dots
questions.solution: The group valence of an element can be determined either by counting the number of dots (valence electrons) or by calculating 8 minus the number of dots.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What equation is used to derive atomic orbitals in wave mechanics?
questions.solution: The atomic orbitals are obtained from the solution of Schrödinger wave equation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is a formal charge in the context of polyatomic molecules or ions?
options: The actual charge on an atom within the molecule
The difference between the number of valence electrons in an isolated atom and the number assigned in the Lewis structure
The total charge of the molecule or ion
The electronegativity of an atom in a molecule
questions.solution: The formal charge of an atom in a polyatomic molecule or ion as the difference between the number of valence electrons of that atom in an isolated state and the number of electrons assigned to that atom in the Lewis structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What effect does the polarizing power of the cation have on the percent covalent character of an ionic bond?
options: It increases the percent covalent character.
It decreases the percent covalent character.
It has no effect on the percent covalent character.
It reverses the percent covalent character.
questions.solution: The polarizing power of the cation is a factor that determines the percent covalent character, suggesting that it increases the covalent character.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which is a molecule where an intermolecular hydrogen bond exists?
questions.solution: An intermolecular hydrogen bond is found in the case of HF (hydrogen fluoride) molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of hybridisation involves the involvement of one s and two p-orbitals?
questions.solution: In sp2 hybridisation, there is involvement of one s and two p-orbitals to form three equivalent sp2 hybridised orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the relative orientation of the p orbitals involved in the pi (π) bond in ethene?
questions.solution: The p orbitals involved in the pi (π) bond are perpendicular to the plane of the molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the ultimate goal of combining atoms in Lewis dot structures?
options: To attain the configuration of noble gases
To attain the configuration of halogens
To attain the configuration of alkali metals
To attain the configuration of transition metals
questions.solution: The combining atoms attain the outer-shell noble gas configurations as a result of the sharing of electrons in Lewis dot structures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What aspect of atoms' valence shells does the theory proposed by Sidgwick and Powell focus on?
questions.solution: The theory proposed by Sidgwick and Powell is based on the repulsive interactions of the electron pairs in the valence shell of the atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is an average bond enthalpy used in the context of polyatomic molecules?
options: To account for changes in temperature
To account for differences in bond length
To account for variations in bond strength
questions.solution: An average bond enthalpy is used in polyatomic molecules to account for variations in bond strength.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What factor primarily contributes to the stabilization of the crystal structure in ionic solids?
options: Energy released in the formation of the crystal lattice
Achieving an octet of electrons around the ionic species in the gaseous state
questions.solution: The crystal structure in ionic solids gets stabilized due to the energy released in the formation of the crystal lattice.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the key concept that Lewis introduced to explain chemical bonding?
questions.solution: Lewis introduced the concept of electron sharing as a key concept to explain chemical bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In what state do ionic compounds exhibit orderly three-dimensional arrangements of cations and anions?
questions.solution: The crystalline state is the state in which ionic compounds exhibit orderly three-dimensional arrangements of cations and anions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the dipole moment of a nonpolar molecule?
options: Equal to the charge of the molecule
Double the charge of the molecule
questions.solution: The dipole moment of a nonpolar molecule is zero.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What important difference between lone pairs and bonding pairs of electrons did Nyholm and Gillespie explain?
options: Bonding pairs are localized on the central atom.
Bonding pairs occupy more space than lone pairs.
Lone pairs are shared between two atoms.
Lone pairs have greater repulsion than bonding pairs.
questions.solution: Nyholm and Gillespie explained that bonding pairs of electrons occupy more space compared to lone pairs of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of forces are involved in the calculation of lattice enthalpy?
options: Only attractive forces between ions of opposite charges
Only repulsive forces between ions of like charge
Both attractive forces between ions of opposite charges and repulsive forces between ions of like charge
questions.solution: The process of calculating lattice enthalpy involves both attractive forces between ions of opposite charges and repulsive forces between ions of like charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of sigma bond is formed between carbon atoms in ethane?
questions.solution: In ethane, a sigma bond of sp3-sp3 type is formed between carbon atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the molecular orbital σ* formed?
questions.solution: The molecular orbital σ* is formed by subtracting the wave function ψ<sub>B </sub>from ψ<sub>A</sub>.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following techniques is NOT a method for measuring bond lengths?
questions.solution: The gravitational techniques are not methods for measuring bond lengths.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the common feature of all Sigma (σ) bonds?
questions.solution: The Sigma (σ) bonds are being formed by head-on or axial overlap of bonding orbitals along the internuclear axis, regardless of the specific atomic orbitals involved.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When is a stage reached where the net force of attraction balances the force of repulsion?
options: When potential energy is at its maximum.
When potential energy is at its minimum.
When the attractive force is less than the repulsive force.
questions.solution: Ultimately a stage is reached where the net force of attraction balances the force of repulsion and the system acquires minimum energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does Lewis postulate about how atoms achieve a stable octet of electrons?
options: By changing the number of neutrons
questions.solution: Lewis postulates that atoms achieve a stable octet of electrons by forming chemical bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What distinguishes the ammonium ion (NH4+) from most cations in ionic compounds?
options: It is composed of metallic elements.
It is composed of non-metallic elements.
It forms anions instead of cations.
questions.solution: The ammonium ion (NH4+) is different from most cations in ionic compounds because it is composed of non-metallic elements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the typical source of anions in most ionic compounds?
questions.solution: Anions in most ionic compounds are derived from non-metallic elements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the implication of the statement, "Even in the case of a covalent bond between two hydrogen atoms, there is some ionic character"?
options: Covalent bonds are always purely covalent.
Hydrogen atoms cannot form covalent bonds.
Covalent bonds may have a small degree of ionic character.
Hydrogen atoms form exclusively ionic bonds.
questions.solution: Even in a covalent bond between two hydrogen atoms, there is some degree of ionic character, indicating that covalent bonds can have a small degree of ionic character.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of bond is formed when two atoms share one electron pair?
questions.solution: When two atoms share one electron pair, they are joined by a single covalent bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the basis of the octet rule?
questions.solution: The octet rule is based upon the chemical inertness of noble gases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the unit of bond dissociation enthalpy?
questions.solution: The unit of bond dissociation enthalpy is "kJ mol-1".

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which noble gases combine with oxygen and fluorine to form compounds?
questions.solution: Noble gases like xenon and krypton combine with oxygen and fluorine to form compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Bond enthalpy is defined as the amount of energy required for what specific action?
options: Forming one mole of bonds between two atoms
Breaking one mole of bonds between two atoms
Changing the state of one mole of bonds
questions.solution: The bond enthalpy is the amount of energy required to break one mole of bonds between two atoms in a gaseous state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the classical concept of bonding, what does an integral bond order of 2 represent?
questions.solution: In the classical concept, an integral bond order of 2 corresponds to a double bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How do ionic compounds in the crystalline state arrange their cations and anions?
questions.solution: The ionic compounds in the crystalline state consist of orderly three-dimensional arrangements of cations and anions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the significance of determining bond lengths in a molecule?
options: It helps in identifying the type of chemical reaction occurring.
It provides information about the bond's stability and energy.
It determines the size of the outermost electron shells.
It measures the distance between valence electrons.
questions.solution: Determining bond lengths in a molecule is significant because it provides information about the bond's stability and energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the direction of the crossed arrow in chemistry related to the conventional direction of the dipole moment vector?
options: The crossed arrow points in the same direction as the dipole moment vector.
The crossed arrow points in the opposite direction to the dipole moment vector.
The crossed arrow has no relation to the dipole moment vector.
The crossed arrow is perpendicular to the dipole moment vector.
questions.solution: The direction of the crossed arrow is opposite to the conventional direction of the dipole moment vector.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the valence shell electronic configuration of nitrogen in the ground state?
questions.solution: The valence shell electronic configuration of nitrogen in the ground state as 1s22s22p1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How are negative and positive ions formed from halogen and alkali metal atoms stabilised?
questions.solution: Kössel's observations state that negative and positive ions formed from halogen and alkali metal atoms are stabilised by electrostatic attraction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the dipole moment of a molecule affected by an increase in charge (Q)?
questions.solution: An increase in charge (Q) in the dipole moment equation μ = Q × r leads to an increase in the dipole moment.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of sigma bond is formed between carbon atoms in ethene?
questions.solution: In ethene, a sigma bond of sp-sp type is formed between carbon atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of force arises between the nucleus of one atom and its own electron?
questions.solution: The attractive forces arise between the nucleus of one atom and its own electron.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How are hybrid orbitals different from pure orbitals?
options: Hybrid orbitals are not used in bond formation.
Hybrid orbitals are used in bond formation.
questions.solution: Unlike pure orbitals, hybrid orbitals are used in bond formation, which distinguishes them from pure orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What term describes molecules and ions that have the same number of electrons?
questions.solution: "Isoelectronic molecules and ions" is used to describe entities with the same number of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of electron pair interaction has greater repulsion: Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) or Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp)?
questions.solution: Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) interaction has greater repulsion than Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp) interaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is hybridization involving 3p, 3d, and 4s orbitals not possible?
options: 3d orbitals have higher energy than 3p and 4s orbitals.
3p orbitals have higher energy than 3d and 4s orbitals.
The energies of 3p and 4s orbitals are comparable.
The energies of 3p orbitals are significantly different from those of 4s orbitals.
questions.solution: No hybridization involving 3p, 3d, and 4s orbitals is possible due to the significant difference in energies between 3p and 4s orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What term is used to describe compounds of elements in and beyond the third period with more than eight valence electrons around the central atom?
questions.solution: The term "expanded octet" is used to describe compounds of elements in and beyond the third period with more than eight valence electrons around the central atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does the VSEPR theory treat resonance structures when determining molecular shape?
options: It considers only one resonance structure.
It averages the shapes of all resonance structures.
It treats each resonance structure separately.
It applies the VSEPR model to any resonance structure.
questions.solution: The VSEPR theory is applicable to any resonance structure when determining molecular shape.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the energy of the bonding orbital compared to the parent orbitals?
questions.solution: The energy of the bonding orbital is lowered compared to the parent orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the relationship between the canonical structures and the resonance hybrid in the concept of resonance?
options: The canonical structures are identical to the resonance hybrid.
The canonical structures are completely different from the resonance hybrid.
The resonance hybrid is a combination of the canonical structures.
The resonance hybrid is used to generate the canonical structures.
questions.solution: The resonance hybrid represents a combination of the canonical structures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the bond between two carbon atoms in an ethene molecule?
questions.solution: In the ethene molecule, the two carbon atoms are joined by a double bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term for the condition where orbitals have the same sign (phase) and orientation in space?
questions.solution: The condition where orbitals have the same sign (phase) and orientation in space as "positive overlap."

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is molecule stability determined based on the occupancy of orbitals?
options: By counting the total number of electrons
By comparing the energy levels of orbitals
By evaluating the ratio of N<sub>b</sub> to N<sub>a</sub>
By analyzing the color of the molecule
questions.solution: The molecule stability is determined by comparing the number of electrons in bonding orbitals (N<sub>b</sub>) to the number in antibonding orbitals (N<sub>a</sub>).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the VSEPR Theory primarily focus on?
options: Predicting the energy levels of electrons
Determining the electronic configuration of atoms
Predicting the geometry of molecules based on electron pair repulsions
Determining the polarity of chemical bonds
questions.solution: The VSEPR Theory primarily focuses on predicting the geometry of molecules based on electron pair repulsions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many sp2 hybrid orbitals of each carbon atom in ethene are used to form sigma bonds with hydrogen atoms?
questions.solution: The two of the three sp2 hybrid orbitals of each carbon atom in ethene are used to form sigma bonds with two hydrogen atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How can the carbon-carbon bond in the ethene molecule be described?
options: sp2-sp2 sigma bond and one pi (π) bond
questions.solution: The carbon-carbon bond in the ethene molecule consists of one sp2-sp2 sigma bond and one pi (π) bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary role of hybrid orbitals in the formation of stable bonds?
options: To minimize electron repulsion and achieve stability
To determine the energy levels of electrons
questions.solution: The main role of hybrid orbitals is to minimize electron repulsion between electron pairs and achieve a stable arrangement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the positive or negative sign on boundary surface diagrams represent?
questions.solution: The positive and negative signs on boundary surface diagrams do not represent charge but instead indicate the sign (phase) of the orbital wave function.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total energy of two molecular orbitals compared to two original atomic orbitals?
questions.solution: The total energy of two molecular orbitals remains the same as that of two original atomic orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of atomic orbitals are involved in p-p overlapping to form a Sigma (σ) bond?
options: A half-filled s-orbital and a half-filled p-orbital
questions.solution: In p-p overlapping, a Sigma (σ) bond is formed between half-filled p-orbitals of the two approaching atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which ion is an exception for forming cations in ionic compounds?
questions.solution: Ammonium ion (NH4+) is an exception because it forms the cation in some ionic compounds despite being composed of two non-metallic elements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is bond order calculated using N<sub>b</sub> and N<sub>a</sub>?
questions.solution: The bond order is half the difference between N<sub>b</sub> and N<sub>a</sub>.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What determines whether a substance is diamagnetic or paramagnetic?
options: The occupation of its molecular orbitals
questions.solution: The occupation of molecular orbitals in a substance determines whether it is diamagnetic or paramagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What should be the energy relationship between the orbitals undergoing hybridisation?
options: They should have significantly different energy.
They should have almost equal energy.
It depends on the type of atom.
questions.solution: The orbitals undergoing hybridisation should have almost equal energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the cation do to the electronic charge of the anion in an ionic bond?
options: The cation reduces the electronic charge of the anion.
The cation increases the electronic charge of the anion.
The cation has no effect on the electronic charge of the anion.
The cation repels the electronic charge of the anion.
questions.solution: The cation polarizes the anion, pulling the electronic charge toward itself and increasing the electronic charge between the two.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What role does the valence shell of an atom play in the process of hybridisation?
options: The valence shell determines the type of hybridisation.
The valence shell provides electrons for hybridisation.
The valence shell determines the energy levels of orbitals.
The valence shell is not relevant to hybridisation.
questions.solution: The valence shell of the atom determines the type of hybridisation that will occur.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which theory provides the geometry of simple molecules?
questions.solution: The VSEPR theory provides the geometry of simple molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term used to describe the energy required to remove electron(s) from a neutral atom?
questions.solution: The energy required to remove electron(s) from a neutral atom is referred to as "ionization enthalpy."

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What factors determine the overlap of orbitals when two atoms come close to form a bond?
options: Sign (phase) and orientation of amplitude of orbital wave function
questions.solution: The overlap of orbitals depends on the sign (phase) and orientation of the amplitude of orbital wave function.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What effect does the polarisability of the anion have on the percent covalent character of an ionic bond?
options: It increases the percent covalent character.
It decreases the percent covalent character.
It has no effect on the percent covalent character.
It reverses the percent covalent character.
questions.solution: The polarisability of the anion is a factor that determines the percent covalent character, suggesting that it increases the covalent character.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens when two hydrogen atoms are at a large distance from each other?
options: There is no interaction between them
questions.solution: When the two hydrogen atoms are at a large distance from each other, there is no interaction between them.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of bonding molecular orbital has larger electron density above and below the internuclear axis?
questions.solution: A pi (π) bonding molecular orbital has larger electron density above and below the internuclear axis, as stated in the paragraph.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the nature of a hydrogen bond compared to a covalent bond?
questions.solution: A hydrogen bond is weaker than a covalent bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is one of the conditions for combining atomic orbitals to form molecular orbitals?
questions.solution: One of the conditions for combining atomic orbitals to form molecular orbitals is that they must overlap to the maximum extent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many molecular orbitals are formed from the combination of 2s and 2p atomic orbitals on two atoms?
questions.solution: The combination of 2s and 2p atomic orbitals on two atoms gives rise to eight molecular orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Is the overall energy change in the formation of NaCl(s) positive or negative?
questions.solution: The energy released in the processes is more than the energy absorbed, meaning the overall energy change is negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What effect does the location of electron density in a bonding molecular orbital have on the repulsion between nuclei?
questions.solution: The location of electron density in a bonding molecular orbital between the nuclei decreases the repulsion between the nuclei of bonded atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which orbitals are suitable for sp hybridisation if the hybrid orbitals are to lie along the z-axis?
questions.solution: The suitable orbitals for sp hybridisation are s and p<sub>z</sub> if the hybrid orbitals are to lie along the z-axis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does the charge on the cation influence the covalent character of an ionic bond?
options: The greater the charge on the cation, the greater the covalent character.
The smaller the charge on the cation, the greater the covalent character.
The charge on the cation has no effect on covalent character.
The covalent character is solely determined by the charge on the anion.
questions.solution: The greater the charge on the cation, the greater the covalent character of the ionic bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the relationship between charge (Q) and distance of separation (r) in the dipole moment equation?
options: Q is inversely proportional to r.
Q is directly proportional to r.
questions.solution: The dipole moment equation μ = Q × r indicates that charge (Q) is directly proportional to the distance of separation (r).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why are hybrid orbitals directed in space in some preferred direction?
options: To maximize electron repulsion between electron pairs
To have a less stable arrangement
To minimize electron repulsion between electron pairs and achieve a stable arrangement
To maximize electron repulsion between atoms
questions.solution: Hybrid orbitals are directed in space in some preferred direction to minimize electron repulsion between electron pairs and achieve a stable arrangement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does the number of nuclei influencing an electron differ between atomic and molecular orbitals?
options: Atomic orbitals are influenced by two or more nuclei, while molecular orbitals are influenced by one nucleus.
Atomic orbitals are polycentric, while molecular orbitals are monocentric.
Both atomic and molecular orbitals are influenced by one nucleus.
Both atomic and molecular orbitals are polycentric.
questions.solution: An electron in an atomic orbital is influenced by one nucleus, while in a molecular orbital, it is influenced by two or more nuclei.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the dipole moment of a polarized molecule?
options: The dipole moment is always zero in a polarized molecule.
The dipole moment is equal to the charge on the molecule.
The dipole moment is the product of charge and distance.
The dipole moment cannot be defined for polarized molecules.
questions.solution: The dipole moment of a polarized molecule is the product of the magnitude of the charge and the distance between the centers of positive and negative charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Who introduced the Valence bond theory?
questions.solution: The Valence bond theory was introduced by Heitler and London.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why are Lewis dot structures considered useful in understanding molecules?
options: They explain the behaviour of all molecules.
They provide a complete picture of bonding.
They help in understanding the formation and properties of molecules to a large extent.
They are simple drawings of molecules.
questions.solution: While Lewis dot structures may not explain the bonding and behaviour of a molecule completely, they do help in understanding the formation and properties of a molecule to a large extent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How do the experimentally determined oxygen-oxygen bond lengths in the O<sub>3</sub> molecule compare to the normal bond lengths for O–O and O=O bonds?
options: They are the same as the normal O–O bond length.
They are the same as the normal O=O bond length.
They are intermediate between the normal O–O and O=O bond lengths.
They are longer than both the normal O–O and O=O bond lengths.
questions.solution: The experimentally determined oxygen-oxygen bond lengths in the O<sub>3</sub> molecule are intermediate between a double and a single bond, indicating they are between the normal O–O and O=O bond lengths.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why can't the 2p<sub>x</sub> or 2p<sub>y</sub> orbitals combine with the 2p<sub>z</sub> orbital of another atom?
questions.solution: The 2p<sub>x</sub> or 2p<sub>y </sub>orbitals cannot combine with the 2p<sub>z</sub> orbital of another atom because they have different symmetries.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term for the partial merging of atomic orbitals that leads to the pairing of electrons?
questions.solution: This partial merging of atomic orbitals is called overlapping of atomic orbitals which results in the pairing of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the dipole moment of a polarized molecule a measure of?
questions.solution: The dipole moment of a polarized molecule is a measure of the molecule's polarity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How are bond lengths typically measured?
options: By calculating the distance between valence electrons
By spectroscopic, X-ray diffraction, and electron-diffraction techniques
By measuring the distance between protons in the nucleus
questions.solution: The bond lengths are typically measured by spectroscopic, X-ray diffraction, and electron-diffraction techniques.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If a molecule has both lone pairs and bond pairs of electrons, which type of interaction will typically result in the greatest repulsion?
options: It depends on the specific arrangement of electron pairs.
questions.solution: The greatest repulsion typically occurs between lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) interactions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of interaction between electron pairs has the highest repulsion?
questions.solution: The repulsive interaction of electron pairs decreases in the order: Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) > Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp) > Bond pair (bp) – Bond pair (bp).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the symbol ∆aH⊖ represent?
questions.solution: The symbol ∆aH⊖ represents the heat of dissociation, as it describes the dissociation of HCl into H and Cl atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the arrow in the molecule's representation indicate about electron density?
options: It represents the absence of electron density.
It signifies the magnitude of electron density.
It denotes the direction of electron density shift.
It illustrates the shape of the molecule.
questions.solution: The arrow in the molecule's representation symbolizes the direction of the shift of electron density.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the significance of the general correlation between bond order, bond enthalpy, and bond length?
options: It helps explain the number of atoms in a molecule.
It helps predict the stability of molecules.
It helps determine the molecular weight of a compound.
It helps identify the temperature at which a bond forms.
questions.solution: The general correlation between bond order, bond enthalpy, and bond length is useful for understanding and predicting the stability of molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What factor affects the covalent character of an ionic bond based on cation size and anion size?
options: The smaller the cation and the larger the anion, the greater the covalent character.
The larger the cation and the smaller the anion, the greater the covalent character.
The charge on the cation and anion has no effect on covalent character.
The covalent character is solely determined by the charge on the anion.
questions.solution: The covalent character of an ionic bond is greater when the cation is smaller and the anion is larger.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the electronic configuration of a Cl atom?
questions.solution: The electronic configuration of a Cl atom as [Ne]3s2 3p5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does the electronegativity of hydrogen compare to that of fluorine?
options: Hydrogen has higher electronegativity than fluorine.
Hydrogen has lower electronegativity than fluorine.
Hydrogen and fluorine have equal electronegativities.
questions.solution: Fluorine has higher electronegativity than hydrogen since it attracts the shared electron pair more strongly in a polar covalent bond like HF.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does bond enthalpy measure?
options: The strength of a chemical bond
The length of a chemical bond
The color of a chemical bond
questions.solution: Bond enthalpy measures the strength of a chemical bond

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is electrovalence defined in the context of ions?
options: It is equal to the atomic number of the ion.
It is equal to the total number of electrons in the ion.
It is equal to the number of unit charge(s) on the ion.
It is equal to the number of neutrons in the ion.
questions.solution: Electrovalence is equal to the number of unit charge(s) on the ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What do atomic orbitals combine to form in the concept of hybridisation?
questions.solution: Atomic orbitals combine to form a new set of equivalent orbitals in the concept of hybridisation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of bond(s) is formed when there are multiple bonds between two atoms in a molecule?
questions.solution: In the formation of multiple bonds between two atoms in a molecule, pi (π) bond(s) are formed in addition to a sigma (σ) bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which atomic orbital can combine with the 2p<sub>z</sub> orbital of another atom?
questions.solution: The 2p<sub>z </sub>orbital of one atom can combine with the 2p<sub>z</sub> orbital of another atom because they have the same symmetry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many double bonds are there between carbon and oxygen atoms in a carbon dioxide molecule?
questions.solution: In the carbon dioxide molecule, there are two double bonds between the carbon and oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the significance of maximizing orbital overlap in molecular orbital formation?
options: It increases electron density between nuclei.
questions.solution: Maximizing orbital overlap is significant because it increases the electron density between the nuclei of a molecular orbital.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is the concept of hybridisation introduced in the context of molecular geometry?
options: To explain the characteristic geometrical shapes of molecules
questions.solution: The concept of hybridisation is introduced to explain the characteristic geometrical shapes of molecules like CH<sub>4</sub>, NH<sub>3</sub>, and H<sub>2</sub>O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the electron pair shared between hydrogen and the strongly electronegative element 'X'?
options: It stays close to the hydrogen atom.
It moves far away from the hydrogen atom.
It moves closer to the hydrogen atom.
questions.solution: When hydrogen is bonded to a strongly electronegative element 'X', the electron pair shared between the two atoms moves far away from the hydrogen atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the central atom in a molecule or complex ion?
options: The atom with the highest electronegativity.
The atom with the lowest electronegativity.
The atom with the most valence electrons.
The atom to which other atoms are bonded.
questions.solution: The central atom in a molecule or complex ion is the atom to which other atoms are bonded, as it plays a central role in the structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which force is stronger, the attractive force or the repulsive force, when two hydrogen atoms form a stable molecule?
options: Attractive and repulsive forces are equal.
questions.solution: Two hydrogen atoms are said to be bonded together to form a stable molecule having the bond length of 74 pm, which implies that the attractive force is strong enough to overcome the repulsive force.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term used to describe a group of atoms with characteristic properties that exist together?
questions.solution: A group of atoms with characteristic properties that exist together is called a molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the van der Waals radius measure in a solid?
options: The size of the atom's core.
The distance between two similar atoms in separate molecules.
The distance between two dissimilar atoms in a covalent bond.
The overall size of the atom including its valence shell.
questions.solution: The van der Waals radius measures the distance between two similar atoms in separate molecules in a solid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Who developed the Valence bond theory further?
questions.solution: The Valence bond theory was developed further by Pauling and others.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the significance of the unit "mol-1" in bond enthalpy?
options: It indicates the number of bonds formed.
It indicates the number of moles of atoms.
It indicates the amount of energy per mole of bonds.
It indicates the temperature at which bonds are broken.
questions.solution: The unit "mol-1" in bond enthalpy represents the amount of energy per mole of bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which type of molecule is an intramolecular hydrogen bond most likely to be found?
questions.solution: Intramolecular hydrogen bonds are most likely to be found in molecules containing highly electronegative elements like fluorine (F), oxygen (O), or nitrogen (N).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the name of the hybridisation type involving the mixing of one s and one p orbital?
questions.solution: The sp hybridisation involves the mixing of one s and one p orbital.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many sp2 hybrid orbitals of a carbon atom overlap axially with the sp2 hybridized orbital of another carbon atom in ethene?
questions.solution: In ethene, one of the sp2 hybrid orbitals of a carbon atom overlaps axially with the sp2 hybridized orbital of another carbon atom to form a C–C sigma bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term used to describe the energy change when an atom gains an electron?
questions.solution: The energy change when an atom gains an electron is referred to as "electron gain enthalpy."

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What was the basis of the explanation provided by Kössel and Lewis for valence?
options: The number of elements in the periodic table
questions.solution: Kössel and Lewis based their explanation of valence on the inertness (lack of reactivity) of noble gases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of bond is formed when combining atoms share three electron pairs?
questions.solution: When combining atoms share three electron pairs, a triple bond is formed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to bond length as bond order increases, according to the general correlation?
questions.solution: The general is that as bond order increases, bond length decreases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What determines the ease of formation of positive and negative ions in the context of ionic compound formation?
options: The atomic mass of the elements
The number of isotopes of an element
The arrangement of electrons in the atoms
questions.solution: The ease of formation of positive and negative ions depends on the arrangement of electrons in the atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the dipole moment of a molecule usually denoted?
questions.solution: The dipole moment of a molecule is usually denoted by the Greek letter 'μ.'

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the Bond Order in the CO molecule?
questions.solution: In CO, there are three shared electron pairs between C and O, resulting in a Bond Order of 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What kind of forces exist between ions of opposite charges?
questions.solution: Attractive forces exist between ions of opposite charges.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the dipole moment of a polyatomic molecule depend on?
options: Only the spatial arrangement of bonds
Only the individual dipole moments of bonds
The spatial arrangement of bonds and individual dipole moments of bonds
The number of atoms in the molecule
questions.solution: The dipole moment of a polyatomic molecule depends on both the spatial arrangement of bonds and the individual dipole moments of bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is an intramolecular hydrogen bond?
options: It is formed within the same molecule.
It is formed between two different molecules of the same or different compounds.
It is formed between two oxygen atoms.
It is formed within the same atom.
questions.solution: An intramolecular hydrogen bond is formed when a hydrogen atom is within the same molecule, typically between two highly electronegative atoms (F, O, N) within that molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of force arises between the nuclei of two atoms?
questions.solution: The repulsive forces arise between the nuclei of two atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For which types of molecules can Lewis dot structures be written?
options: For both identical and different molecules
questions.solution: The Lewis dot structures can be written for other molecules also, in which the combining atoms may be identical or different.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How do the two sp hybrid orbitals point in relation to each other along the z-axis?
options: They point in the same direction.
They point at right angles to each other.
questions.solution: The two sp hybrid orbitals point in the opposite direction along the z-axis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the difference in  ∆aH⊖ values for the O – H bonds in polyatomic molecules indicate?
options: The difference in the number of atoms
questions.solution: The difference in  ∆<sub>a</sub>H⊖ values for the O – H bonds in polyatomic molecules indicates a change in bond strength due to the changed chemical environment.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What knowledge is required for a discussion of the Valence bond theory?
options: The overlap criteria of atomic orbitals
questions.solution: The discussion of the Valence bond theory is based on the knowledge of atomic orbitals, electronic configurations of elements, the overlap criteria of atomic orbitals, and the principles of variation and superposition.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the bond angle defined as?
options: The angle between the orbitals containing non-bonding electron pairs around the central atom.
The angle between the orbitals containing bonding electron pairs around the central atom.
The angle between the orbitals containing valence electrons in a molecule.
The angle between the orbitals containing all electron pairs in a molecule.
questions.solution: The bond angle Is the angle between the orbitals containing bonding electron pairs around the central atom in a molecule or complex ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary difference between bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals?
options: Bonding orbitals are filled, while antibonding orbitals are empty.
Bonding orbitals have lower energy and greater stability.
Bonding orbitals are formed from s orbitals, while antibonding orbitals are formed from p orbitals.
Antibonding orbitals are always fully occupied.
questions.solution: The bonding molecular orbitals have lower energy and greater stability compared to antibonding molecular orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the mean or average bond enthalpy calculated in polyatomic molecules?
options: By dividing the total bond dissociation enthalpy by the number of bonds broken
By counting the total number of atoms
questions.solution: The mean or average bond enthalpy in polyatomic molecules is obtained by dividing the total bond dissociation enthalpy by the number of bonds broken.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the molecular orbital formed by the subtraction of atomic orbitals called?
questions.solution: The molecular orbital formed by the subtraction of atomic orbitals is called the antibonding molecular orbital.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is represented by a double-headed arrow in the context of resonance?
questions.solution: In the context of resonance, a double-headed arrow represents the presence of resonance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the energy change associated with the formation of a hydrogen molecule?
questions.solution: The energy gets released when the bond is formed between two hydrogen atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the order of decreasing repulsion for electron pair interactions?
options: Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp) > Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) > Bond pair (bp) – Bond pair (bp)
Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) > Bond pair (bp) – Bond pair (bp) > Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp)
Bond pair (bp) – Bond pair (bp) > Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) > Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp)
Bond pair (bp) – Bond pair (bp) > Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp) > Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp)
questions.solution: The repulsive interaction of electron pairs decreases in the order: Lone pair (lp) – Lone pair (lp) > Lone pair (lp) – Bond pair (bp) > Bond pair (bp) – Bond pair (bp).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the general principle for selecting the lowest energy Lewis structure?
options: The one with the largest formal charges on the atoms.
The one with the smallest formal charges on the atoms.
The one with the most atoms.
The one with the fewest lone pairs.
questions.solution: Generally, the lowest energy structure is the one with the smallest formal charges on the atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does a positive electrovalence indicate for an ion?
options: It has an equal number of protons and electrons.
questions.solution: A positive electrovalence indicates that an ion has lost electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What term is used to describe the distribution of electrons among various molecular orbitals?
questions.solution: The distribution of electrons among various molecular orbitals is called the electronic configuration of the molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which type of molecules is the octet rule not satisfied for all the atoms?
options: Molecules with an even number of electrons
Molecules with an odd number of electrons
questions.solution: In molecules with an odd number of electrons like nitric oxide (NO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO<sub>2</sub>), the octet rule is not satisfied for all the atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many types of covalent bonds are there?
questions.solution: There are two types of covalent bonds: Sigma (σ) bond and pi (π) bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the main characteristic of the hydrogen atom in a hydrogen bond?
questions.solution: The hydrogen atom in a hydrogen bond becomes partially positively charged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the Bond Order in a molecule with two shared electron pairs between its atoms?
questions.solution: O<sub>2</sub> has two shared electron pairs and a Bond Order of 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Is the promotion of electrons to higher energy levels a necessary condition prior to hybridisation?
options: It depends on the type of atom.
questions.solution: The promotion of electrons to higher energy levels is not an essential condition prior to hybridisation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the Lattice Enthalpy of NaCl?
questions.solution: The Lattice Enthalpy of NaCl is 788 kJ mol-1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary focus of Lewis symbols in representing electrons?
questions.solution: Lewis symbols are primarily used to represent valence electrons in an atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do lone pair electrons in a molecule occupy more space than bonding pairs?
options: Because lone pairs have a stronger attraction to the central atom.
Because bonding pairs are shared between two atoms.
Because bonding pairs have greater repulsion.
Because lone pairs are localized on the central atom.
questions.solution: Lone pair electrons occupy more space because each bonding pair is shared between two atoms, leading to greater repulsion between lone pairs.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does the mutual repulsion of electrons in an antibonding molecular orbital compare to the attraction between the electrons and the nuclei?
questions.solution: In an antibonding molecular orbital, the mutual repulsion of electrons is stronger than the attraction between the electrons and the nuclei, resulting in a net increase in energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary purpose of indicating formal charges on atoms in Lewis structures?
options: To represent real charge separation within the molecule.
To track the valence electrons in the molecule.
To determine the electronegativity of the atoms.
questions.solution: Indicating the charges on the atoms in the Lewis structure helps in keeping track of the valence electrons in the molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is a key characteristic of hybridised orbitals in terms of their energy and shape?

They have equivalent energies but different shapes.
They have equivalent energies and shapes.
They have different energies but equivalent shapes.
questions.solution: The hybridised orbitals are always equivalent in energy and shape.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

They tend to occupy the same region in space.
They tend to move away from each other.
They tend to form chemical bonds.
questions.solution: The VSEPR theory states that pairs of electrons tend to occupy positions in space that minimize repulsion, which maximizes the distance between them.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

By transferring valence electrons or by sharing valence electrons
questions.solution: According to the electronic theory of chemical bonding, atoms can combine either by transferring valence electrons or by sharing valence electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Who introduced notations to represent valence electrons in an atom?
questions.solution: G.N. Lewis, an American chemist, introduced notations to represent valence electrons in an atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the net charge of polyatomic ions typically treated in Lewis structures?
options: It is assigned to the central atom.
It is ignored in Lewis structures.
It is divided equally among all atoms in the ion.
It is assigned to a particular atom.
questions.solution: The net charge of polyatomic ions is not assigned to a particular atom in Lewis structures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What do negative and positive ions formed from halogen and alkali metal atoms attain in terms of electronic configuration?
questions.solution: According to Kössel, negative and positive ions formed from halogen and alkali metal atoms attain a stable noble gas electronic configuration, typically an octet of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry

options: The repulsion effects between electron pairs
questions.solution: Nyholm and Gillespie refined the VSEPR model by explaining the important difference between the localization of lone pairs and bonding pairs of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the attractive force that holds various constituents together in different chemical species called?
questions.solution: The attractive force that holds various constituents together in different chemical species is called a chemical bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term for the state in the formation of a hydrogen molecule where two hydrogen atoms are closest together and their atomic orbitals partially overlap?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What occurs during the formation of an antibonding molecular orbital?
options: The electron waves cancel each other.
The electron waves reinforce each other.
The electron waves combine into a single wave.
questions.solution: During the formation of an antibonding molecular orbital, the electron waves cancel each other due to destructive interference.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.solution: A polar covalent bond is formed when there is a significant electronegativity difference between two atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How did Lewis picture the atom in terms of its structure?

As a positively charged 'Kernel' and an outer shell
As a cube with eight electrons
questions.solution: Lewis's picture of the atom as consisting of a positively charged 'Kernel' (nucleus plus inner electrons) and an outer shell.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.solution: In MO theory, the electron probability distribution around a group of nuclei in a molecule is described by molecular orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

options: Understanding the properties of covalent compounds
Understanding the properties of metallic compounds

Understanding the properties of organic compounds
questions.solution: Kössel's postulations provide the basis for understanding ion-formation by electron transfer and the formation of ionic crystalline compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How can the formation of molecular orbitals be qualitatively understood?
options: Through the interference of electron waves
Through the angular momentum of electrons
questions.solution: The formation of molecular orbitals can be qualitatively understood in terms of the constructive or destructive interference of the electron waves of the combining atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What effects result from the repulsion between electron pairs in molecules?
questions.solution: The repulsion effects between electron pairs in molecules result in alterations in bond angles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What role does the ionization enthalpy play in the stability of an ionic compound?

It contributes to the energy absorbed.
It is compensated for by the electron gain enthalpy.
It is not relevant to the stability of ionic compounds.
questions.solution: The ionization enthalpy contributes to the energy absorbed, but the primary factor for stability is the energy released in the formation of the crystal lattice.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the weak π bond formed in ethene?

By axial overlap of unhybridized orbitals
By axial overlap of p orbitals
By axial overlap of s orbitals

questions.subject: Chemistry

options: The number of electrons in the bond
The number of bonds between two atoms in a molecule
The distance between two atoms in a molecule
questions.solution: In the Lewis description of a covalent bond, the Bond Order is given by the number of bonds between the two atoms in a molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the composition of the ammonium ion (NH4+)?
options: Made up of two metallic elements
Made up of two non-metallic elements
Made up of one metallic and one non-metallic element

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.solution: Pi (π) molecular orbitals are not symmetrical around the bond-axis in the sigma-pi nomenclature.

The number of hybrid orbitals is equal to the number of atomic orbitals that get hybridised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the relationship between bond enthalpy and bond formation?

Bond enthalpy remains constant during bond formation.
Bond enthalpy increases during bond formation.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Higher lattice enthalpy leads to greater stability of ionic compounds.
Reason (R) : Lattice enthalpy is a direct measure of the electrostatic forces of repulsion among the constituent ions in an ionic solid.
The correct answer is
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct, but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct, but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A): Higher lattice enthalpy leads to greater stability of ionic compounds. This statement is correct. Lattice enthalpy is the energy released when gaseous ions combine to form one mole of a solid ionic compound. A more negative (higher in magnitude) lattice enthalpy signifies a stronger attraction between ions and thus a more stable ionic compound.
Reason (R): Lattice enthalpy is a direct measure of the electrostatic forces of repulsion among the constituent ions in an ionic solid. This statement is incorrect. Lattice enthalpy is a measure of the strong electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions in the crystal lattice, not repulsion.
Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct, but the Reason (R) is incorrect. The correct option is (3).

questions.solution: The correct order of covalent character is $\mathrm{NaCl} \lt  \mathrm{LiCl} \lt  \mathrm{MgCl}_2 \lt  \mathrm{BeCl}_2$. The covalent character depends on small size as well as more + ve charge on cation.
